title: Run the default agent on another machine
head: 136b0078767e
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new args metadata converts the no-argument default-agent getter into CLI help
leads.consequence: `omarchy default agent` no longer prints the selected agent, even though its metadata examples still recommend it. The direct binary and menu guards continue to return the value; routed getter users instead see the usage page and exit 0, so callers reading stdout can mistake help for an agent name.

leads.summary: The feature does not ensure an SSH client is installed
leads.consequence: The default package lists explicitly ship tmux but do not list openssh; the runtime package does not require it. On a machine without an incidental openssh dependency or prior SSHD setup, `ssh -G` fails open and the launched terminal runs a nonexistent ssh binary, closing without the promised unreachable-host notification. Add/ensure the client dependency or report its absence before launching.
leads.triage: dropped: openssh absent from package lists verified by rg, but whether it arrives transitively was not established; low value

leads.summary: Returning from a remote-only agent does not provision its local installation
leads.consequence: Selecting an agent with a host set skips local installation; clearing the host only removes the host file. If that agent is absent locally (for example Hermes without the preinstall, or after removing preinstalls), the next agent key/`--local` fails rather than bringing it back. The new test changes the selected agent to pi before testing the switch back, hiding this case. The user must reselect the agent to install it locally.
leads.triage: dropped: confirmed from source (clearing host is rm -f; selection with host skips install) but the local error message already tells the user to reselect; low value

leads.summary: Preflight rejects a usable existing SSH master connection
leads.consequence: An established ControlMaster connection can still carry SSH sessions after direct TCP to its listening port becomes unavailable. This helper ignores the configured master and treats a five-second direct TCP timeout as unreachable, so no terminal is launched and no attempt to reuse the healthy socket is made. This also contradicts the helper's stated fail-open intent for answers it cannot determine.
leads.triage: dropped: narrow scenario (master alive while direct TCP fails); not confirmed independently

leads.summary: `omarchy agent stop` kills manually created sessions sharing its predictable prefix
leads.consequence: The code has no ownership marker or executable check, only a session-name prefix. On the SSH account, any user-created tmux session named `omarchy-agent-personal` is selected by an unqualified stop and killed, destroying its windows and processes. The comment that a session someone else opened is not ours to kill is contradicted by the filter.
leads.triage: dropped: prefix-based selection of omarchy-agent-* sessions is the stated contract; low value

leads.summary: The stop command exits successfully after every kill fails
leads.consequence: The `if ssh ...; then ... else echo ...; fi` leaves a zero-status echo as the last command in the loop. Even if all remote tmux kills fail, `omarchy agent stop` exits 0, causing scripts to believe all sessions ended. It also suppresses SSH stderr, so only the generic error remains on screen; subsequent invocation tries to kill the same sessions again.
leads.triage: published within stop-status note; confirmed by coordinator source read

leads.summary: OpenClaw is not launchable on an SSH host that has OpenClaw but not Omarchy
leads.consequence: Unlike other agents, the wrapped remote command invokes `omarchy-launch-openclaw --tui`, not `openclaw`. A Linux workstation with a working OpenClaw CLI but no Omarchy binary cannot launch it. The feature docs say the host is whatever SSH understands, and the default setter skips the local install, without documenting that this agent also requires an Omarchy installation and its OpenClaw gateway setup on the remote host.

leads.summary: A long valid host name makes the fixed SSH ControlPath fatal
leads.consequence: The socket name includes full expanded `%r@%h:%p` inside the runtime directory. For long but valid DNS names (or long runtime paths), it exceeds the Unix-domain socket path limit; OpenSSH fatals with `ControlPath too long` rather than falling back to a fresh connection. The successful reachability probe is then followed by a terminal that closes on every launch. A bounded `%C` hash avoids the name-dependent failure.

leads.summary: An empty host file means local to the launcher but remote to the selector
leads.consequence: The getter returns an empty host for a zero-byte or blank-first-line file, so `omarchy-agent` runs locally, but selecting an agent tests only `-f` and skips its installation. On installs/dotfiles that create an empty setting to mean local, selection succeeds and launches a missing agent. Test `-s` or read the normalized value used by the launcher.
leads.triage: dropped: empty host file not produced by the PR's own setter (--host '' removes it); edge case

leads.summary: With the overlapping directory PR, remote launches ignore the configured project directory
leads.consequence: Open #9350 adds a persisted agent-directory to select a project and still starts the local process there. Applying its diff to this head retains the hardcoded remote `~/Work` redirect, so a host user configuring a custom project starts or resumes the Work session, not the chosen project; neither PR's tests notices. GitHub currently marks #9350 CONFLICTING, so this is an integration concern upon resolving the textual conflict, not a claim it will merge automatically.
leads.triage: published as related open PR note; verified by coordinator (gh pr view, 9350.diff) and Opus self-check

leads.summary: The new reachability helper is completely shadowed by the tests
leads.consequence: The tests use a stub that decides reachability from an environment flag, not from `ssh -G` or the TCP check. A plausible one-token bug in hostname extraction causes unreachable direct hosts to skip the probe and reach the launcher, while every current test still passes. Add a separate fixture with fake `ssh -G` output and a stub for TCP timeout that asserts alias hostname/port, proxies, and failure cases.
leads.triage: overlaps Opus F4 coverage note (probe mocked); not published separately

leads.summary: A tmux listing failure is reported as 'No agent session'
leads.consequence: The remote `tmux list-sessions` stderr is dropped and its nonzero status is converted to success by `... | grep ... || true`. When a session cannot be enumerated (broken server, denied socket, wrong tmux socket), SSH still succeeds and the caller tells the user no agent session is running, leaving running work untouched. Preserve failures distinct from a successful empty list.
leads.triage: published within stop-status note; confirmed by coordinator source read

leads.summary: The new panel paragraph assumes the remote and local logins use the same subscription
leads.consequence: Account-wide rate limits or balances only represent remote spending when the remote user signs in to the same provider account as the local collector. Merely setting an SSH host never forwards or verifies the account. With different remote credentials the bar continues to show the local account and can claim available budget despite exhaustion on the remote. Say 'if both machines use the same account' and note sync requires a producer on each machine.

limits: Cross-PR search returned 450 unique open PRs, only 33 high-signal candidates had file inventories fetched; 12 topical diffs were read and #9350 was applied/tested. Other open PR interactions are not ruled out.

The PR's SSH/tmux command was not connected to a real host. OpenSSH V_10_2_P1 and tmux 3.5a source and isolated stub fixtures establish the reported boundary behavior. Exact shipped package versions on a particular installation are not pinned by this repository.

flags.claim: This continues until `omarchy agent stop` ... The manual's "the same initial prompt as it would get here" holds only for the first launch.
flags.why: The session also ends when the agent inside it exits. tmux destroys a pane whose program exits when remain-on-exit is off (the default), and the session goes with its only pane. Omarchy's tmux.conf does not set remain-on-exit. Prompts are dropped only while a session exists. After the agent is quit, or after stop, the next launch creates a new session and gets its prompt. My final.md F1 has the same imprecision ('persist by design until omarchy agent stop').

flags.claim: Prompts can break for users who set tmux's default-shell to a non-POSIX shell.
flags.why: Wrong criterion and lost qualifier. What matters is whether the shell supports $'...': fish lacks it, and so does dash before 0.5.13, which is a POSIX sh. Also, only prompts that bash renders as $'...' are affected (a newline or another control character), as line 34 correctly says.

flags.claim: a variant checked in the same setup avoids both layers
why: The variant was checked only with a bash login shell: the recording wrapper execs /bin/bash.
It removes the $'...' form from the ssh string and any shell inside tmux.
The ssh string is still parsed by the account's login shell. fish treats \' and \\ inside single quotes as escapes.
In the variant's string for the tested prompt, a single-quoted region ends in a backslash right before its closing quote ('...second \'\''quoted...'). fish would read that as an escaped quote.
So for fish logins, the variant should fix plain prompts (the quoted regions contain no backslashes) but not prompts with backslashes or multi-line prompts with an apostrophe. This part was not run.
My final.md F2 says 'removes both dependencies', which is equally too strong.

flags.claim: gives tmux the argv as separate words, and tmux then execs it without a shell.
flags.why: Nit. This is true for commands of two or more words. A one-word command, `pi` with no prompt (command=(pi)), still reaches tmux as a single argument and runs through default-shell -c. That is harmless for a bare word.

flags.claim: Killing the agent session, which is what `omarchy agent stop` does, moved the agent window into another tmux session instead of detaching it.
why: Lost qualifier: this happens only when another tmux session is running on that host. With detach-on-destroy off, tmux looks for another session and detaches if none exists.
The run had an unrelated session named `mine`.
It also happens when the agent exits, not only on stop.
The suggestion (set detach-on-destroy on for the agent's session) is supported by source: the option is session-scoped, and server-fn.c:444 reads the destroyed session's own option. It was not run.

flags.claim: Having the mock run `cat >/dev/null` unless `-n` is passed would make the "every session" assertion guard the fix it describes.
why: The PR test calls omarchy-agent-stop without redirecting stdin (test lines 1025, 1034, 1043, 1049).
The list call has no -n, so the mock's `cat` would read the test's inherited stdin. From a terminal it blocks until EOF.
My check fixture also ran stop with </dev/null.
My final.md F4 has the same omission.

flags.claim: A full `test/cli` plus `test/shell.d` run fails the same files on the `quattro` tip and on the merge, so the PR adds no new failures. / the full `test/cli` and `test/shell.d` suite ... were run
why: All 269 files ran on both the tip and the merge, and the failure sets are identical.

test/cli stopped at its line 580-581 (vscode theme) on both sides, and 11 shell files stopped at environment failures on both sides (for example, a missing omarchy-pkgs checkout). Assertions after those points ran on neither side.
None of the 12 failing files references the PR's files, so the conclusion stands. 'Full' just slightly overstates the coverage.

flags.claim: the launch and stop paths against a simulated far side (bash 5.3, real tmux 3.7c, OpenSSH 10.5p1, ssh stubbed)
flags.why: Nit, misattribution inside the parenthetical. The simulated far side used no OpenSSH (ssh was stubbed or emulated). OpenSSH 10.5p1 was used for `ssh -G` in the probe run and for the ControlPath check.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Checked at head `136b0078`, and on a merge with the current `quattro` tip.

**Verified:** when every remote layer is bash, the remote launch delivers a prompt containing quotes, a newline and `$(...)` as one literal argument, and nothing in it runs. The reachability probe resolves `~/.ssh/config` aliases and skips ProxyJump and ProxyCommand as described. `--local` and the crash pinning work, and local launches with no host set are unchanged. `test/shell.d/default-agent-test.sh` passes at the head and on the merge. A run of all `test/cli` and `test/shell.d` files fails the same files on the `quattro` tip and on the merge, so the PR adds no new failures.

There are three issues: a second launch silently drops its prompt, the quoting assumes bash at two remote layers, and bare `omarchy default agent` now prints help.

### A second launch drops its prompt and any agent change

The remote script runs `cd ~/Work` and names the session `omarchy-agent-${PWD##*/}`. That name is always `omarchy-agent-Work`, or `omarchy-agent-<home dir name>` without `~/Work`. It then runs `tmux new-session -A` ([`bin/omarchy-agent:187-193`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/bin/omarchy-agent#L187-L193)). When the session already exists, `-A` attaches to it and ignores the command argument (tmux `cmd-new-session.c`). This was run with the PR's real `omarchy-agent` building the command, and a simulated far side running bash and real tmux 3.7c:

```text
launch                                             result
1  claude, "Review this project"                   session omarchy-agent-Work created, agent started
2  claude, a different multi-line prompt           attached as 2nd client; prompt never reached an agent
3  default switched to codex, "Fix the tests"      attached as 3rd client; pane still claude, codex never started
```

**Impact:** after the first launch, `omarchy agent prompt "..."` and the agent key reopen the old conversation and discard the new prompt. This lasts while that session exists, until the agent is quit inside it or `omarchy agent stop` ends it, and nothing tells the user. Changing the default agent has no effect on that host during that time either. The manual's "the same initial prompt as it would get here" ([`manual/17-ai.md:39`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/manual/17-ai.md?plain=1#L39)) holds only when no session is running on that host. The test only checks that `new-session -A -s` appears in the script.

**Suggested change:** some possible approaches:
- Include the agent in the session name.
- When a prompt is given, start a new, uniquely named session instead of attaching.
- Detect an existing session and report that the prompt was not delivered.

Whichever is chosen, document the attach behavior in the manual.

### The remote command assumes bash-style parsing at two layers

- **ssh layer:** `remote_command` contains newlines, so `${remote_command@Q}` always produces `$'...'`. All four command builds that were checked started with `bash -lic $'`. sshd hands that string to the remote account's login shell. fish has no `$'...'` syntax (its own "fish for bash users" guide says so), so on a host whose login shell is fish, every launch fails. `omarchy agent stop` builds `bash -lc ${remote@Q}` the same way ([`bin/omarchy-agent-stop:43`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/bin/omarchy-agent-stop#L43)) and fails there too.
- **tmux layer:** the code comment and the PR description say tmux hands its argument to `sh`. tmux actually runs a single-string command with its `default-shell` (tmux 3.7c `spawn.c`), which comes from `$SHELL`, the passwd entry or `tmux.conf`. In the run, tmux invoked the far side's `$SHELL` with `-c` and the quoted agent command. A remote user whose tmux `default-shell` is fish would see prompts that are quoted as `$'...'` (multi-line prompts, for example) break inside tmux, even with a bash login shell.

The test evaluates every layer with bash `eval`, so neither dependency shows up in it. This was not run against a real fish or zsh account. The conclusion rests on the `$'` form observed in the built command and on the shells' documentation and source.

**Impact:** remote agents do not work for accounts whose login shell is fish. Multi-line prompts can break for users whose tmux `default-shell` has no `$'...'` quoting, such as fish.

**Suggested change:** a variant checked in the same setup (with a bash login shell) removes the `$'...'` form from the ssh command and the shell inside tmux:

```bash
  remote_command="[[ -d ~/Work ]] && cd ~/Work; session=omarchy-agent-\${PWD##*/}; session=\${session//[^[:alnum:]_-]/-}; if tmux -V >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec tmux new-session -A -s \"\$session\" $agent_command; fi; exec $agent_command"
```

With the script on one line, `${remote_command@Q}` uses plain single quotes. Passing the already-quoted `$agent_command` without `@Q` gives tmux the argv as separate words, and tmux then execs a multi-word command without a shell. tmux has supported this form since 2.0, and its manual notes that it "can avoid issues with shell quoting". In that run, the prompt `first line\nsecond 'quoted' "double" $(touch pwned) back\slash` arrived intact and nothing ran. On a fish login shell this should help plain prompts, but fish treats `\'` and `\\` inside single quotes as escapes, so prompts with backslashes may still break there (not run). The test's line-by-line parsing of the script would need to be updated to match. Separately, `bash -lic` always reads bash startup files, so a zsh or fish user whose mise activation lives in `~/.zshrc` or `config.fish` does not get it. The manual's "found the same way it is here" ([`manual/17-ai.md:41`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/manual/17-ai.md?plain=1#L41)) is worth qualifying for that case.

### `omarchy default agent` with no arguments prints help

The new metadata is `omarchy:args=[pi|...|muse] | --host [<[user@]host>]` ([`bin/omarchy-default-agent:4`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/bin/omarchy-default-agent#L4)). `command_requires_args` in [`bin/omarchy:361-372`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/bin/omarchy#L361-L372) strips the bracketed groups, and the leftover `|--host` counts as a required argument, so the dispatcher shows help.

```text
omarchy default agent      parent: claude      head / merge with quattro: Usage ... Arguments ... Examples
```

**Impact:** the command's own first example no longer prints the current agent. Calling `omarchy-default-agent` directly (as the menu and scripts do) is unaffected.

**Suggested change:** `[pi|...|muse] [--host [<[user@]host>]]` or `[pi|...|muse|--host [<[user@]host>]]`. Both evaluate as optional with the dispatcher's own function.

### Smaller notes

- **Session end on an Omarchy far side:** Omarchy's [`config/tmux/tmux.conf:77`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/config/tmux/tmux.conf#L77) sets `detach-on-destroy off`. When another tmux session is running on that host, killing the agent session (which is what `omarchy agent stop` does) moved the agent window into that other session instead of detaching it. A run without that config detached. Setting `detach-on-destroy on` on the agent's own session should avoid it (from tmux source, not run).
- **ControlPath length:** `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/omarchy-agent-ssh-%r@%h:%p` ([`bin/omarchy-agent:207`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/bin/omarchy-agent#L207)) expands the user and the full host name. A long FQDN produced 118 bytes, and ssh exited immediately with "ControlPath too long". OpenSSH also adds a random suffix to the listener's path, so somewhat shorter names can fail after authentication (inferred from the source, not run). `%C` keeps the path short and fixed-length.
- **`omarchy agent stop` status:** a failed `tmux list-sessions` is discarded (`2>/dev/null ... || true`, [`bin/omarchy-agent-stop:39`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/bin/omarchy-agent-stop#L39)) and reported as "No agent session is running". The script also exits 0 when every kill fails. Listing uses `bash -lc` while launch uses `bash -lic`. If tmux is only on the interactive PATH, stop could therefore report no session while one is running (from source, not run).
- **Stop example:** `omarchy agent stop omarchy-agent-work` ([`bin/omarchy-agent-stop:5`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/bin/omarchy-agent-stop#L5)) does not match the real session name `omarchy-agent-Work`. The match is exact (`grep -Fx`), so that example reports no session.
- **Agents panel wording:** Claude limits are read from this machine's `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, and Codex limits come from a local `codex app-server`. The manual's "still account for everything the remote agent spends" ([`manual/17-ai.md:45`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/136b0078767e4482d4acf3d738fa71135a3f8ede/manual/17-ai.md?plain=1#L45)) therefore holds only when the same account is also signed in locally. This comes from reading the collectors; the panel was not rendered.
- **Optional test improvement:** the test's `ssh` mock never reads stdin. With `ssh -n` removed from `omarchy-agent-stop`, the whole test file still passes. A stub that reads stdin like real ssh shows the mutant ending only the first of two sessions. Having the mock run `cat >/dev/null` unless `-n` is passed, with the test's `omarchy-agent-stop` calls given `</dev/null`, would make the "every session" assertion guard the fix it describes.
- **Related open PR:** #9350 ("Make the default agent directory configurable") replaces the local `~/Work` redirect with a configurable directory. This PR hardcodes `~/Work` on the remote side, so combining the two would need a decision about what the remote side should use.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** head `136b0078`, parent `2fbac0c8` and a merge with `quattro` tip `25ead28f`. Source inspection of the changed scripts, their callers, the dispatcher, the tmux config and the usage collectors, plus the OpenSSH, tmux, bash and fish source or documentation relevant to the claims. The PR's test file, all `test/cli` and `test/shell.d` files, test mutants, the real reachability probe against synthetic `ssh -G` configurations (OpenSSH 10.5p1), and the launch and stop paths against a simulated far side (bash 5.3, real tmux 3.7c, ssh stubbed) were run in an isolated sandbox. `test/cli` and some environment-dependent shell tests stop early in the sandbox, identically with and without the PR. No real ssh connection was made. Real remote hosts, fish or zsh login shells and the agents panel were not exercised.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
